plan: Given my value of $39, I should bid just below my value to maximize profit while ensuring a win. Since values are drawn uniformly, bidding slightly less than my value, say $38.9, could prevent overbidding risk. Rational bidders will aim to bid slightly under their value, so my bid should be competitive but not exceed my value.

Given my value of $27, I aim to bid slightly below it to maximize potential profit while ensuring a competitive bid. A rational strategy involves bidding slightly less than my value to win without overpaying. Assuming others bid rationally, they will not exceed their value. I will bid $26.9 to try and win while paying the second-highest bid, optimizing my profit.

Given my value for the prize is $13, I should bid slightly below this to maximize profit while maintaining a chance to win. Bidding exactly $13 risks zero profit if I win. Bidding much lower risks losing the auction. A bid around $12.5 balances these considerations, ensuring I only win if competitors bid less, thereby maximizing potential profit.
